extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V . Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated by filtering existing BIG-Bench tasks based on specific criteria to arrive at a clean, challenging, and tractable subset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from the BIG-Bench collaborative benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were filtered to remove those with more than three subtasks, fewer than 103 examples, no human-rater baselines, non-multiple-choice/exact match metrics, models beating human raters, and extremely difficult tasks. A random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken for most tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually composed three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The human-rater scores are not fully representative of human performance. The formatting and content of some tasks changed multiple times, and task descriptions were sometimes hard to follow.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capabilities and limitations of large language models, specifically testing chain-of-thought prompting on challenging tasks.

name.evidence: In this work, we focus on a suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks which we call BIG-Bench Hard (BBH ).

description.evidence: We select a subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks and group them into an evaluation suite referred to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) , which we make publicly available.

url.evidence: The data, prompts, and the Codex model outputs are all available at https://github.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard .

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We analyze BIG-Bench by identifying tasks for which the highest reported model performances are below the average human-rater score. We select a subset of 23 particularly challenging tasks and group them into an evaluation suite referred to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: In this paper, we curate BIG-Bench Hard (BBH ), a subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: BIG-Bench is a collaborative benchmark that aims to quantitatively measure the capabilities and limitations of language models (Srivastava et al., 2022, Beyond the Imitation GameBench mark).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: These filtering criteria result in 78 clean multiple-choice or exact-match tasks... For all but three tasks in BBH, we take a random subset of 250 evaluation examples.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We manually compose three chain-of-thought exemplars for each task in BBH; all the prompts used are shown in Section C.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: the organizers acknowledge that one should be careful in interpreting these results because the scores are not fully representative of human performance... In some cases, the task description was hard to follow and could have been better-formulated.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We use the remaining 23 tasks as our curated benchmark that we refer to as BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)... we explore whether chain-of-thought prompting (CoT; Wei et al., 2022b) achieves better performance on BBH.
